messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: Advisory: brief suppression observed for long-context responses (us-east)

Hi Sarah / Ben —

I wanted to let you know we're observing a short-lived suppression of longer generated responses for hosted inference in the us-east region. Symptoms reported: truncated/early-stopped generations when requests include long contexts (roughly > 2k tokens). The window of impact we see in telemetry is approximately 07:50–08:10 UTC for a subset of capacity behind our us-east routing.

What we know so far:
- Impact: intermittent early termination or reduced completion length for long-context generation requests.
- Scope: small percentage of requests routed through one pool in us-east; your traffic shows ~0.8% of requests affected in that window.
- User-visible effect: shorter completions or "..." truncation rather than errors.

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Routed new requests from affected pools to healthy capacity to reduce customer impact.
- Applied a temporary mitigation to reduce aggressive KV cache prefetching on the affected nodes.
- Opened an ops bridge and engineering is triaging root cause.

Suggested short-term workarounds for LuminaHealth until we confirm full resolution:
- Reduce max_tokens for long-context calls where possible.
- Trim system-level context or move less-critical context into a secondary call.

I've attached a short incident snapshot with sample traces and a minimal request sample for our engineers (incident-snapshot-20261030.txt). We'll follow up with an ETA as soon as we have a working remediation.

Link to the live incident: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-10-30-longgen-suppression

Apologies for the disruption — I know this behavior can be disruptive for flows that depend on long completions. I'm standing by for questions and will keep you updated.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Aditya — short update from triage (ops bridge notes below).

On Fri, Oct 30, 2026 at 08:35, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Forwarding Lumina's reply. They are asking about data exposure (PHI) and want an ETA + credit ask.

Root cause hypothesis (preliminary):
- We observed a race condition between our KV-prefetch path and an aggressive garbage collection window on a subset of inference servers. That race caused the generation engine to see an empty/partial KV cache for ongoing long-context generations, which leads to early stopping behavior rather than an outright error.
- No evidence that request payloads were exfiltrated or written to external third-party stores. All affected debugging traces remained in ephemeral host logs / internal traces; access is limited to ops+eng. We will perform a full audit to confirm.

Mitigation applied (09:00 UTC):
- We disabled the aggressive prefetching on the affected fleet and rerouted traffic; this restored expected completion lengths for the majority of traffic.
- We also applied a conservative backstop to the KV eviction logic while we prepare a code patch.

Timing & next steps:
- Full patch (race fix + improved prefetch backoff) is targeted for deploy at 14:00 UTC today.
- We will run a canary for 30 minutes then stage rollout to remaining nodes.
- Postmortem write-up will be posted to the incident page within 48 hours; a deeper security audit confirming no PHI exposure will be included.

Please share the statements below with Lumina:
- We currently see no evidence of data exposure outside ephemeral logs.
- We have mitigated the observable user impact by disabling prefetch on affected nodes and rerouting traffic.
- Patch deploy targeted for 14:00 UTC with staged rollout; we will confirm successful completion and follow up with a postmortem + security audit.

If Lumina would like a short technical call with an engineer, I can hop on at 10:00 UTC.

—Jonas
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah / Ben —

Follow-up with a full update after engineering triage.

Summary:
- Root cause: a race between KV prefetch and an internal GC window caused partial KV state for some long-context generations.
- Data exposure: engineering's preliminary audit finds no evidence of payloads being written to external systems; traces are limited to ephemeral host logs. We will publish a formal security audit in the postmortem.
- Mitigation: temporary measures and routing reduced impact within an hour; the targeted patch was deployed at ~14:05 UTC and rolled out in stages.
- Compensation: we will apply a one-time service credit to LuminaHealth for the impacted window. I will confirm the credit amount and formal SLA impact by end of day tomorrow.

Next steps:
- Postmortem and security audit posted to the incident page (https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-10-30-longgen-suppression) within 48 hours.
- Optional 30-minute technical call with Jonas if you want a deeper walkthrough — we've penciled in 10:00 UTC but can move to your availability.

Apologies again for the disruption. We know reliability is critical for your workflows and appreciate the quick flag. If you'd like me to escalate an immediate credit or to schedule the postmortem review with your compliance team, say the word and I'll coordinate.
